name: Asin: making salt on the coast
description: Salt (asin) was made on the coast by evaporating seawater in beds or by boiling, and traded inland; with it fish was salted and fermented into paste (bagoong).
sources: William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994)
Francisco Ignacio Alcina, Historia de las islas e indios de Bisayas (1668), trans. Cantius Kobak and Lucio Gutiérrez (UST Publishing House, 2002–2005)

lore.en: Coastal people made salt by letting seawater dry in shallow beds, or by boiling brine, and traded it inland for rice, forest goods and gold. Salt preserved the catch: salted fish and fermented fish paste (bagoong) kept for months in clay jars.
lore.fil: Gumagawa ng asin ang mga tao sa baybayin sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatuyo ng tubig-dagat sa mababaw na kama, o pagpapakulo ng tubig-alat, at ipinagpapalit ito sa looban kapalit ng palay, produkto ng gubat at ginto. Pinapanatili ng asin ang huli: tumatagal nang ilang buwan sa banga ang inasnang isda at bagoong.

inGame.en: An Asinan makes Asin on the shore. Each house uses Asin to salt fresh food into its jars, so it doesn't spoil. Asin is kept in the Kamalig.
inGame.fil: Gumagawa ng Asin ang Asinan sa dalampasigan. Ginagamit ng bawat bahay ang Asin para asnan ang sariwang pagkain at ilagay sa banga, para hindi masira. Sa Kamalig iniimbak ang Asin.
